summary: Robert Alexander Neil was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Aberdeen under William Duguid Geddes and at Peterhouse, Cambridge. He served as University Lecturer in Sanskrit at Cambridge from 1884 and Fellow at Pembroke College in 1900.

Robert Anthony Orsi works in religious studies and history. He studied at Trinity College and Yale. He held posts at Fordham, Indiana University, Harvard, Northwestern (chair in Catholic Studies from ~2007), and Notre Dame (Faculty Fellow 2020–2021).

Robert B. Ekvall worked in Tibetology and related fields. He was a research associate at the University of Chicago (~1953–1958), a research fellow at the University of Washington (1958), and honorary curator at the Burke Museum (~1965–1983).

Robert Baker Aitken was a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar. He studied at the University of Hawaiʻi and UC Berkeley, trained under various teachers including Daisetsu Teitaro Suzuki, and held posts at Hawaiʻi and the East-West Center (~1960–1969).

Robert Barnett is a scholar of Tibetology who studied at the University of Cambridge. He held positions at Columbia University (~1999–2018), Tibet University (2000–2006), SOAS (~2018), and King's College London (~2019).

Robert Caesar Childers was an Indologist and linguist who studied Buddhist literature. Educated at Oxford and under Yatramulle Dhammarama Thera, he served as Sub-Librarian at the India Office (1872) and professor of Pali at University College London (~1872–1876).

Robert Chalmers was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Oriel College, Oxford, and under T. W. Rhys Davids. He served as president of the Royal Asiatic Society (1922–1925) and Master of Peterhouse, Cambridge (1924–1931).

Robert Chambers was an Indologist and legal scholar educated at Lincoln College, Oxford. He served as Vinerian Professor of English Law at Oxford (1766), Chief Justice at Fort William (~1789–1798), and president of The Asiatic Society (~1794–1798).

Robert Charles Zaehner specialized in religious studies, Iranian, and Indology. He studied at Christ Church and Cambridge under Harold Walter Bailey. At Oxford, he taught Persian (1950) and Eastern Religions and Ethics (1952), holding a fellowship at All Souls (~1952–1974).

Robert DeCaroli is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and archaeology. He earned his MA and PhD at UCLA under Robert L. Brown, lectured at UCLA and Loyola Marymount, and joined the faculty at George Mason University in ~1999.

Robert Deliège is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at the University of Oxford (~1980–1984). He held posts at the University of Kerala and became a professor at Université catholique de Louvain in ~1989.

Robert Duquenne was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He served as a specialist in Tantric Buddhism at Hōbōgirin (attested 1981) and held a post at the École française d'Extrême-Orient (attested 2009).

Robert E. Buswell Jr. is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at UC Berkeley under Lewis Lancaster and others. He served as a professor and later Distinguished Professor Emeritus of Asian Languages & Cultures at UCLA from ~1986 to 2022.

Robert E. Harrist, Jr. is a scholar of Sinology and art history. He has held academic posts at Columbia University, where he served as Jane and Leopold Swergold Professor Emeritus of Chinese Art History (attested 2009 and 2026).

Robert E. Morrell was a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies who studied under Robert H. Brower and William H. McCullough. He held an academic post at Washington University in St. Louis (attested 1985 and 2006).

Robert E. Svoboda is an Indologist who studied at the University of Oklahoma (~1970–1972) and under Aghori Vimalananda. He served as an adjunct member at The Ayurvedic Institute, Bastyr University, and the Institute for Religion and Health (attested 2008).
Robert F. Rhodes is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He pursued doctoral studies at Harvard University and served as a professor at Otani University (attested 1993–2000 and 2012–2014).

Robert Florida is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He served as Dean of Arts and Professor of Religion at Brandon University and later as an Emeritus Fellow at the University of Victoria (attested 2000–2005).

Robert Ford Campany is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies. He held academic posts at Indiana University Bloomington (~1989–2006), the University of Southern California (~2006–2010), and Vanderbilt University (2010).

Robert Gardner was a scholar who earned his bachelor's degree at Harvard (~1943–1947). He taught at the University of Puget Sound (~1950–1953) and served as a professor at Harvard University from 1956 to 1997.
